final_answer:
Let \(z=x+iy=re^{i\theta}\). Since

\[
x^4-6x^2y^2+y^4=r^4\cos 4\theta,\qquad
x^6-15x^4y^2+15x^2y^4-y^6=r^6\cos 6\theta,
\]

we get

\[
P=r^6(a+\cos 4\theta),\qquad Q=r^6(b+\cos 6\theta).
\]

The system is

\[
\dot z=(-P+iQ)z,
\]

so in polar coordinates

\[
\dot r=-r^7(a+\cos 4\theta),\qquad
\dot\theta=r^6(b+\cos 6\theta).
\]

Introduce \(d\tau/dt=r^6\) for \(r>0\). Then

\[
\frac{dr}{d\tau}=-r(a+\cos4\theta),\qquad
\frac{d\theta}{d\tau}=b+\cos6\theta.
\]

If \(|b|\le 1\), the angular equation has equilibria satisfying \(\cos6\theta=-b\). Along such rays, stability requires

\[
a+\cos4\theta>0
\]

for every solution of \(\cos6\theta=-b\). Otherwise some ray is non-decaying or repelling.

If \(|b|>1\), \(\theta\) rotates around the circle. Then the radial decay rate is governed by the angular average

\[
\overline A
=
\frac{\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{a+\cos4\theta}{b+\cos6\theta}\,d\theta}
{\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{1}{b+\cos6\theta}\,d\theta}.
\]

Now

\[
\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{\cos4\theta}{b+\cos6\theta}\,d\theta=0
\]

because the Fourier modes are incompatible, so \(\overline A=a\). Thus for \(|b|>1\), global asymptotic stability is equivalent to

\[
a>0.
\]

For \(|b|\le1\), the worst possible value of \(\cos4\theta\) subject to \(\cos6\theta=-b\) must be found. Let \(u=2\theta\). Then

\[
\cos6\theta=\cos3u=4\cos^3u-3\cos u=-b.
\]

Also

\[
\cos4\theta=\cos2u=2\cos^2u-1.
\]

Let \(c=\cos u\). The constraint is

\[
4c^3-3c=-b.
\]

We need

\[
a+2c^2-1>0
\]

for every real root \(c\in[-1,1]\) of that cubic. Equivalently,

\[
a>1-2c^2
\]

for all such roots. Therefore the exact answer is:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
|b|>1,\quad a>0,\\[2mm]
|b|\le1,\quad a>1-2c^2\text{ for every }c\in[-1,1]\text{ with }4c^3-3c=-b.
\end{cases}
}
\]

These and only these pairs \((a,b)\) make \((0,0)\) globally asymptotically stable.
